problem: name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE compares case-sensitively, so one tag exists in several spellings (sample: PYTHON id 25, Python id 28, python id 19390; 20 names in three spellings). queries/tag_id.sql returns only the lowest id, so /tag/python shows 171 of the 592 bookmarks carried by the three spellings, while queries/related_tags.sql uses all three ids and lists the other spellings as related tags. README says all spellings are one page. The binary UNIQUE index also cannot serve the NOCASE lookups.
fix: Merge case variants onto the lowest id (remap bookmark_tag with INSERT OR IGNORE, delete old bookmark_tag and tag rows), then rebuild the table with name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE and change schema.sql the same way. Tested on a copy of marks.db with SQLite 3.53.1: 29,960 tags remain, id 25 carries 592 bookmarks, both lookups become index SEARCH. Tag-creating code must look up case-insensitively before insert.

problem: WHERE name = :tag COLLATE NOCASE has no matching index (the UNIQUE index on tag.name is binary), so EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows SCAN tag: every tag page reads all ~450,000 tag rows before fetching bookmarks, growing with tag count.
fix: Structural: make tag.name COLLATE NOCASE (see tag); the query then uses SEARCH on sqlite_autoindex_tag_1 and can stay as written. Stopgap that leaves the split tags: CREATE INDEX tag_name_nocase ON tag(name COLLATE NOCASE);

problem: The case-insensitive name filter cannot use an index, and on the sample the plan is SCAN bt USING COVERING INDEX bookmark_tag_by_tag, i.e. ~30 million bookmark_tag rows checked against the tag lookup on every tag page.
fix: Same collation change on tag.name; the plan then becomes SEARCH tag (name=?), SEARCH bt (tag_id=?), SEARCH bt2 USING PRIMARY KEY (bookmark_id=?). The CREATE INDEX tag_name_nocase stopgap gives the same plan.

problem: For the largest tag (~40,000 bookmarks, ~3.75 tags per bookmark) the self-join touches about 110,000 rows and sorts a GROUP BY on every view of that tag page, although the result only changes when bookmarks are tagged.
fix: After indexing the lookup, measure the largest tag; if too slow, store the top 20 per tag (e.g. tag_related(tag_id, other_tag_id, together)) maintained by the code that writes bookmark_tag, or cache by tag id.
